input: I enjoy cooking because it helps me unwind after a busy day. I usually makes simple meals with fresh vegetables, and I like sharing them with my family. It is a relaxing way to spend time together.
question: Do you enjoy cooking?

key_issues.message: 主谓一致错误：'I usually makes' 应为 'I usually make'。
'It is a relaxing way to spend time together' 中 'to spend time together' 略显正式，口语中更自然的是 'for us to spend time together' 或 'to spend time together as a family'。

feedback.optimization_summary: 修正了主谓一致错误，并将结尾短语调整为更自然的口语表达，整体内容保持不变。
feedback.final_upgraded_answer: I enjoy cooking because it helps me unwind after a busy day. I usually make simple meals with fresh vegetables, and I like sharing them with my family. It's a relaxing way for us to spend time together.
feedback.reference_answer: To be honest, I wouldn't say I love cooking, but I do enjoy it under the right circumstances. My enjoyment really depends on who I'm cooking for. When I'm just making something for myself, I tend to see it as a bit of a chore—I'll grab whatever's quick, like eggs on toast or instant noodles. But when I'm cooking for other people, it's a completely different story. I get a real kick out of planning a menu, picking out fresh ingredients, and then seeing everyone enjoy what I've made. There's something deeply satisfying about that. For instance, last month I hosted a small dinner for a few friends and made a slow-cooked beef stew. Watching them go back for seconds made all the effort worthwhile. So I suppose my answer is: I enjoy cooking, but mainly as a social activity rather than a daily routine.

feedback.reference_answer: Honestly, I have a love-hate relationship with cooking. On weekdays, when I'm exhausted after work, I just want something quick, so I often rely on takeaways or simple pasta. But on weekends, I genuinely enjoy it—it's almost therapeutic for me. I love the whole process of chopping vegetables, smelling the herbs, and watching a dish come together. It's like a creative outlet where I can experiment with new recipes without any pressure. For example, last Sunday I tried making a Thai green curry from scratch, and even though it wasn't perfect, the sense of accomplishment was really rewarding. So I'd say I enjoy it, but only when I have the time and energy to truly savor it.

feedback.reference_answer: Actually, I've come to enjoy it, but that wasn't always the case. When I first moved out on my own, I saw cooking as a chore—I'd just boil pasta or microwave ready meals because I had no confidence in the kitchen. But over the past couple of years, I've started to see it differently. It's become a way for me to unwind after a long day, especially when I put on some music and take my time with the prep. I also love the social side of it—inviting friends over and cooking for them gives me a real sense of pride. That said, I'm not into fancy or complicated dishes; I stick to simple, hearty meals that I know will turn out well. So yes, I genuinely enjoy it now, mainly because it's become more about connection and relaxation than just feeding myself.
feedback.reference_angle_summary: 以时间变化为主线：从讨厌做饭到享受做饭，原因是它从任务变成了放松和社交的方式，并强调只做简单可靠的菜。
